cohort: The study included 546 very-low-birth-weight (VLBW) premature infants, excluding those with a history of meningitis or early neonatal sepsis.
finding: Late-onset sepsis (LOS) was significantly associated with alterations in neurodevelopment at 25 months of age, including a decrease in Mental Development Index, and an increased risk of mild motor disorders, moderate cognitive delay, and cerebral palsy.
